decision_framework.title: Database Concurrency and Locking Strategy
decision_framework.context: Choosing between Optimistic Locking, Pessimistic Locking, and In-Memory Sequencing under concurrent writes, while avoiding the Single-Node Distributed Systems Fallacy.

branch.condition: Low-to-medium contention mutations where conflicts are rare (e.g. editing document title, updating user profile)
branch.recommendation: Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) with version number
branch.trade_offs: Zero lock overhead on reads, high throughput; trade-off: client must handle retry on OCC conflict.
branch.anti_pattern: Do not use SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on low-contention read-heavy endpoints.

branch.condition: High-contention critical balance/inventory deductions where conflict probability is high (e.g. debiting user credits, reserving ticket)
branch.recommendation: Pessimistic Row-Level Locking (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) inside short database transaction
branch.trade_offs: Guarantees sequential correctness without retry storms; trade-off: locks database rows, latency spikes if transaction is slow.
branch.anti_pattern: Never hold external network I/O calls (e.g. Stripe, LLM APIs) while holding a pessimistic row lock.

branch.condition: Multi-pod backend web services deployed behind a Load Balancer (Single-Node Fallacy)
branch.recommendation: Database-Level Locking (SELECT FOR UPDATE / Serializable) or Distributed Lock (Redis Redlock)
branch.trade_offs: Guarantees cross-instance consistency across all Kubernetes pods; trade-off: slight network latency to DB / Redis.
branch.anti_pattern: CRITICAL ANTI-PATTERN: Never use an in-memory Node.js Promise Mutex or local Map as a concurrency control mechanism for production multi-instance services. Pod A cannot see Pod B's RAM mutex.

branch.condition: Ultra-high-frequency real-time event streaming and orderbook matching (MarketStrategies trading terminal, 10,000+ ticks/sec)
branch.recommendation: Single-Threaded Event Loop with In-Memory Ring Buffer and Async DB Flush
branch.trade_offs: Zero database lock contention, sub-millisecond execution; trade-off: state must be reconstructed from WAL / Domain Events upon crash.
branch.anti_pattern: Never route tick-by-tick trading updates through relational database row transactions.
